hero.heading: Flaherty Dental Laboratory, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built October 3, 2026, from flahertydentallab.com, including the history and services pages, and from public metal prices. No federal index is used, and this page says why. Every number is labeled; the assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: (exact: $4,112 and $66,944) Rounding to the nearest $5,000 overstates the low end, so the exact figures govern.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Units you ship in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per thousand units.

constants.text: Metal drift uses the public gold price, $4,177 on October 1, 2026 against $3,864 a year earlier (+8.1 percent) [[BENCHMARK]], applied only to units that carry metal. Zirconia and resin have no public curve and are charged nothing.

model.disclosure: This model carries no federal index: none maps onto a dental laboratory.

terms.label: Unbilled planning in the new lines
Metal drift on units that carry metal

model.formulaText: Moved per 1,000 units = 1,000 × remake share × remake cost + 1,000 × new-line share × planning hours × hourly rate + 1,000 × metal share × metal value × 0.081
model.plainText: In words, the remakes doctors send back at their full cost, plus the planning hours the new lines absorb without a line on the invoice, plus the slice of this year's gold rise carried by the units that hold metal.
model.callout: What nobody counts at a laboratory your size is which line pays. Forty years of removables and crowns, and beside them three new lines, each with its own hours, materials, remakes, and a price set against companies a thousand times your size. The planning behind a guide or an aligner case appears on no invoice; it appears in your evenings. A small laboratory cannot afford one line that quietly takes the hours the others need.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: A family laboratory since 1982 that tells its history in one line, immigrants who built a future through diligence, and then proves it: casts, flexible dentures, crowns, metal frameworks, and orthodontic appliances, everything made in this country [[OBSERVED]].

In the last few years you added three lines most laboratories your size will not touch: clear aligners, sleep appliances under a certification you earned, and implant planning with surgical guides [[OBSERVED]].
A dentist writes that you and Alex communicate well, shade in the laboratory, and turn a case fast when she is in a pinch [[OBSERVED]].

proposal.heading: What we propose
proposal.lead: The proposal: the line count (two quarters by product line, the three new lines kept apart), the decision page in your words, and the first month run on it, counted; fixed fee between $1,200 and $1,800; read-only; no patient information leaves the building.
